steps.description: Implement the algebraic independence hypothesis test by writing a Python script that: (1) Defines a set of analytical constraint functions (e.g., polynomials, trigonometric combinations) that form the "bootstrap" constraints; (2) Varies the number of constraints w (sample size); (3) For each w, performs a width scan on small feedforward networks (1 hidden layer, ReLU activation) to find the minimum width N_c that achieves zero violation (max absolute error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraint points; (4) Records training and validation errors at each width; (5) Determines if the system is "rigid" (finite N_c that saturates as w increases) or "fat" (N_c grows indefinitely or remains unbounded). The script will use PyTorch for network implementation and NumPy for constraint generation and evaluation.

plans.objective: [DIM: measure] The minimal network width $N_c(w)$ required for zero violation follows a logarithmic scaling $N_c(w) \propto \log_2(w)$ for rigid constraint sets, as the information-theoretic capacity of a single hidden layer network grows linearly with width while the constraint entropy grows logarithmically; predict: $N_c(w) = \lceil \log_2(w) \rceil$ for $w \in [4, 16]$; pro: grounded in VC-dimension theory and information capacity of shallow networks; con: may not hold if constraints are redundant or structured.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] This is a pure ML/math hypothesis test concerning network capacity and constraint sets. The previous DFT-based attempt failed because it was the wrong domain (physical vs. abstract). I will implement the experiment from scratch in Python: generate a rigid constraint set (e.g., a low-degree polynomial or smooth function), train single-hidden-layer ReLU networks of varying widths N, measure the minimum width N_c(w) that achieves zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out points, and compare against the logarithmic prediction N_c(w) = ⌈log₂(w)⌉. I'll also test the "con" case (redundant/structured constraints) to see if the scaling breaks. The output will be a table of w, N_c(w), and observed trend.
